rounds.prompt: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
___ the rain, we went for a walk.
The hotel was expensive. ___, the food was excellent.
rounds.note: However starts a new sentence and takes a comma.

rounds.prompt: The match was cancelled ___ the storm.
I was tired, ___ I went to bed early.
She saved money ___ she could travel.
rounds.note: Purpose + a clause with can / could → so that.

rounds.prompt: You won't pass ___ you study.
Take an umbrella ___ it rains.
rounds.note: In case = because it might happen.

rounds.prompt: My sister loves cooking, ___ I prefer eating out.
rounds.note: Whereas compares two different people or things.

rounds.prompt: It was ___ a good film that we watched it twice.
The film was ___ good that we watched it twice.
He's intelligent. ___, he's very hard-working.
rounds.note: Moreover adds a point in the same direction.

rounds.prompt: Despite ___ (be) tired, she finished the race.
In spite of ___ (have) little money, they travelled a lot.
She got up early in order ___ (catch) the first bus.
I'll call you as soon as I ___ (arrive).
rounds.note: After as soon as, a present tense for the future.

rounds.prompt: We'll stay here until the rain ___ (stop).
rounds.note: After until, a present tense for the future.

rounds.prompt: Take a jacket in case it ___ (get) cold.
He spoke quietly so as not ___ (wake) the baby.
Unless you ___ (hurry), you'll miss the train.
rounds.note: Unless + present simple (already negative in meaning).

rounds.prompt: It was such ___ (cold) day that the lake froze.
By the time we ___ (arrive), the film had started.
rounds.note: By the time + past simple, then past perfect.

rounds.context: A contrast, followed by a clause.
rounds.line: ___ she was tired, she kept running.

rounds.context: A contrast, followed by a noun.
A reason, followed by a noun.

rounds.line: It was late, ___ we took a taxi.
You can borrow my bike ___ you bring it back.
Tomás loves football, ___ Diogo prefers tennis.
The flat is cheap. ___, it's near the beach.

rounds.prompt: Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Build the sentence.
Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: Although it was cold, we swam.
Despite it was cold, we swam.
Even though it was cold, we swam.
rounds.answer: Despite it was cold, we swam.
rounds.note: Despite + noun or -ing, never a clause.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: The trains were late because of the snow.
The trains were late because it snowed.
The trains were late due to the snow.
The trains were late because the snow.
rounds.answer: The trains were late because the snow.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: It was so hot that we stayed inside.
It was such a hot day that we stayed inside.
It was so hot day that we stayed inside.
The day was so hot that we stayed inside.
rounds.answer: It was so hot day that we stayed inside.
rounds.note: So + adjective; such + a + adjective + noun.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: I'll wait until you come back.
I'll call you as soon as I arrive.
I'll tell her when I will see her.
We'll leave when the rain stops.
rounds.answer: I'll tell her when I will see her.
rounds.note: After when, a present tense: when I see her.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: He's rich. However, he's not happy.
He's rich, but he's not happy.
He's rich; nevertheless, he's not happy.
He's rich. Although, he's not happy.
rounds.answer: He's rich. Although, he's not happy.
rounds.note: Although joins two clauses; it can't start a sentence alone like however.

rounds.prompt: Three are correct. Tap the one that isn’t.
options: I went there to buy bread.
I went there in order to buy bread.
I went there for buy bread.
I went there so that I could buy bread.
rounds.answer: I went there for buy bread.
rounds.note: Purpose with a verb: to buy, never for buy.

rounds.prompt: Contrast or reason?
rounds.note: Contrast turns the idea; reason explains it.

rounds.prompt: What follows each one?
rounds.note: Prepositions take a noun; conjunctions take a clause.

rounds.prompt: Result or purpose?
rounds.note: A result is what happened; a purpose is what someone wanted.

rounds.prompt: Addition or contrast?
rounds.note: Addition continues the idea; contrast turns it.

rounds.prompt: Condition or time?
rounds.note: Conditions say if; time linkers say when.

rounds.prompt: Match each linker to its job.
Match each linker to what follows it.
pairs: a clause with can / could / would
rounds.note: The linker decides the grammar after it.

rounds.prompt: Match each formal linker to its everyday equivalent.
rounds.note: Formal linkers for essays and reports.

rounds.prompt: Match each linker to its meaning.
Although it rained, we enjoyed the trip.
We didn't go out because the weather was bad.
She left early so that she wouldn't miss the bus.
rounds.stem: She left early ___ miss the bus.
rounds.note: So that … wouldn't → in order not to.

rounds.prompt: If you don't hurry, you'll be late.
The coffee was so hot that I couldn't drink it.
rounds.stem: It was ___ that I couldn't drink it.

rounds.prompt: Although he had studied, he failed.
Take a map because you might get lost.
rounds.note: Because it might happen → in case.

rounds.prompt: She's clever and she's also very kind.
rounds.note: And also → not only … but also.

rounds.sentence: Despite it was raining, we went out.
rounds.note: Before a clause: although. Or keep despite and use a noun: despite the rain.

rounds.sentence: The flight was delayed because the fog.
I'll phone you when I will get home.
rounds.note: After when, a present tense for the future.

rounds.sentence: However it was late, we kept talking.
She went to the shop for buy some milk.
rounds.note: Purpose with a verb: to buy.

rounds.sentence: Unless you don't study, you won't pass.
In spite of he was tired, he kept working.
rounds.note: In spite of + noun or -ing, or although + clause.
